title: Adhyaya 4: Phala (The Fruit of Realization)
summary: Explores the destruction of past karma, the departure of the soul, the path of light, and the state of liberation (Moksha).
ai_summary: Badarayana concludes the masterpiece by describing the unconditioned majesty and eternal freedom of the liberated soul.

verses.translation: Repetition of spiritual contemplation is necessary, because scripture instructs it repeatedly.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: Until direct realization (Aparoksha Anubhuti) is unveiled, hearing, reflection, and meditation (Sravana, Manana, Nididhyasana) must be repeated.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: आत्म-साक्षात्कार की प्राप्ति तक ध्यान और मनन की निरंतर आवृत्ति करनी चाहिए।

verses.translation: On attaining Brahman, future sins do not cling to the sage and past sins are dissolved, as declared in scripture.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: Just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, karmic residue cannot taint the illuminated soul.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: ज्ञान की प्राप्ति होने पर पूर्व संचित पाप नष्ट हो जाते हैं और आगामी कर्म लिप्त नहीं होते।

verses.translation: At the departure of life, speech merges into the mind, as seen from experience and testified by scripture.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: The senses withdraw inward: speech merges in mind, mind in Prana, and Prana in the inner Self.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: उत्क्रमण काल में वाणी मन में लीन होती है, मन प्राण में और प्राण आत्मा में।

verses.translation: The meditating soul proceeds along the solar path of the rays of light (Archiradi Marga), which is well-known in all scriptures.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: The Devayana path leads step by step toward the higher realms of light and gradual liberation (Krama Mukti).

layers.author: ramanujacharya
layers.content: उपासक अर्चिरादि देवयान मार्ग से परम पद को प्राप्त होता है।

verses.translation: Attaining the Supreme Light, the liberated soul manifests in its own essential nature, as signified by the words 'in its own form'.

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: Moksha is not the acquisition of something novel, but the unveiled manifestation of the soul's innate non-dual divinity (Svarupa Avirbhava).

layers.author: adi-shankara
layers.content: मुक्त आत्मा किसी नए रूप को नहीं, अपितु अपने वास्तविक नित्य चैतन्य स्वरूप में प्रतिष्ठित होती है।
